Done. Summary:

**Cause** — In `Collector.delete()` (`django/db/models/deletion.py`), the fast-path optimization for a single object with no dependencies (lines ~274–280) ran `sql.DeleteQuery(model).delete_batch([instance.pk], ...)` and returned immediately — never touching the instance. The normal (non-fast) path at the bottom of the method does clear PKs via `setattr(instance, model._meta.pk.name, None)` after `query.delete_batch(...)`, so only the fast path left the stale PK behind.

**Fix** — one line added to the fast path, mirroring the normal path:

```python
if self.can_fast_delete(instance):
    with transaction.mark_for_rollback_on_error():
        count = sql.DeleteQuery(model).delete_batch([instance.pk], self.using)
    setattr(instance, model._meta.pk.name, None)   # ← added
    return count, {model._meta.label: count}
```
